rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that divorced women must receive maintenance.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على وجوب النفقة للمطلقات

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه وأبو علي
rows.claim: An irrevocably divorced woman is entitled to maintenance and lodging; this is the Hanafi view and Abu Ali's choice, against al-Shafi'i.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي حنيفة وأصحابه، واختيار أبي علي، خلاف ما يقوله الشافعي

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar refused to abandon scripture and the Prophet's Sunna for Fatima bint Qays's report that the Prophet gave her no maintenance or lodging, saying she may have erred.
rows.anchor: قال عمر: لا ندع كتاب ربنا وسنة نبينا بقول امرأة لعلها وهمت، يعني فاطمة بنت قيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard of what is recognized as proper excludes both extravagance and stinginess.
rows.anchor: بالمعروف على أنه ليس فيه إسراف ولا تقتير؛ لأن ذلك لا يكون من المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clarifies the verses so the legally accountable person can learn; “so that you reason” means “so that you know.”
rows.anchor: والغرض أن يعلم المكلف؛ لأن قوله: (لعلكم تعقلون) لكي تعلموا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab reports abrogation by the rule assigning half the stipulated dower; Jishumi says his interpretation entails no abrogation.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد بن المسيب أن الآية منسوخة بقوله فنصف ما فرضتم، وعلى ما حملنا لا نسخ في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage urges jihad and warns against disobeying God in it; jihad was prescribed for earlier peoples and belonged to earlier prophets' laws.
rows.anchor: الحث والترغيب في الجهاد، والتحذير من مخالفة أمر الله فيه، وعلى أن الجهاد كان من فرائض من كان قبلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihad requires a leader and organizer to unite the community.
rows.anchor: الجهاد يحتاج إلى مدبر وأمير يجمع الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kingship may be separate from prophethood, and a prophet may, by God's permission, assign kingship to another.
rows.anchor: وتدل على جواز أن ينفصل الملك من النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets may reinforce their people's covenants about required duties, as the wording “هل عسيتم” does here.
rows.anchor: للأنبياء تشديد العهود والمواثيق على أممهم فيما يلزمهم؟ فلذلك قال: (هل عسيتم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A community may disobey even after emphatic confirmation of its commitment.
rows.anchor: المخالفة قد تقع من الأمة مع التوكيد البليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abandoning battle after it has been prescribed is injustice and a major sin.
rows.anchor: ترك القتال بعدما كتب عليهم ظلم؛ لأنه كبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abandoning jihad brings afterlife punishment, strengthens the enemy, and risks defeat; the same harms follow leaving evil unopposed, so removing evil is obligatory.
rows.anchor: جميع ذلك يحصل في ترك إزالة المنكر، فلذلك وجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting earlier prophets and their miracles, Jishumi presents these reports as a transition establishing Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم من أنباء الرسل ومعجزاتهم عقبه بالتنبيه على نبوة نبينا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier events are God's proofs, truthfully recited to Muhammad; his detailed account without reading books or mixing with learned people is evidence of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: حيث أخبر عن جميع ذلك بأوضح بيان من غير أن قرأ كتابا وخالط أحدا ممن هو من أهل المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier prophets' reports and miracles had become lost, so their confirmation rests on Muhammad's prophethood and report.
rows.anchor: لأن أخبارهم ومعجزاتهم قد اندرست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier prophets were established by revelation; Muhammad also received revelation, so there is no basis for distinguishing his prophethood from theirs.
rows.anchor: وقد أوحي إليه كما أوحي إليهم فلا معنى للفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Declaring Muhammad a messenger calls him to undertake his mission after the proof has been established.
rows.anchor: الاستدعاء إلى القيام وبما أرسل به بعد قيام الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the signs wisdom, proof, and benefit; making Muhammad a messenger likewise serves wisdom and benefit.
rows.anchor: نصب تلك الآيات حكمة وحجة ومصلحة، كذلك جعلك رسولا لما فيه عن المصلحة والحكمة

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: “Those messengers” refers to the prophets previously mentioned in scripture.
rows.anchor: من تقدم ذكرهم من الأنبياء في الكتاب، عن أبي علي وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm takes “those” to mean the messengers through whom corruption was repelled.
rows.anchor: الرسل الذين أرسلهم، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads the verse as consoling Muhammad: those messengers suffered from their peoples as he did.
rows.anchor: أن تلك الرسل نالهم من قومهم مثل الذي نالك من الأذى، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Equality in prophethood does not require equality in rank; God favored some messengers over others.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتوهم أحد أن التسوية في النبوة تقتضي التسوية في الفضل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God favored some messengers over others just as He favored Muhammad over them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كما فضلناك عليهم فضلنا بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distinctive stations include God speaking with Moses and Muhammad's mission to all jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: كلامه مع موسى وإرساله محمدا إلى الكافة الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means “God spoke to him”; Jishumi compares it to “تشتهي الأنفس,” meaning “the souls desire it.”
rows.anchor: يعني كلمه الله كقوله: (تشتهي الأنفس) أي تشتهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Raised some in degrees” means assigning higher stations according to deeds and interests.
rows.anchor: يعني منازل لبعضهم فوق بعض على قدر أعمالهم، وعلى قدر المصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proofs given to Jesus are the miracles and the scripture he received.
rows.anchor: الحجج وهو ما آتاه من المعجزات والكتاب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the Holy Spirit as Gabriel and al-Quddus as God.
rows.anchor: الروح جبريل والقدس الله تعالى، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Holy Spirit as the name by which Jesus revived the dead.
rows.anchor: الاسم الذي كان يحيي به عيسى الموتى، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim takes it as the pure spirit breathed into Mary, which brought Jesus forth unlike other human beings.
rows.anchor: هو الروح الطاهرة التي نفخت فيها فأتت به من بين سائر بني آدم، عن أبي مسلم

words: وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا ٱقْتَتَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ
rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God could have coerced people and prevented fighting, but instead gave them choice and made them responsible.
rows.anchor: مشيئة الإكراه أي لو شاء أن يجبرهم ويمنعهم عن القتل لفعل، ولكن خيرهم وكلفهم ولم يجبرهم، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Rabi identify those who fought later as people after Moses and Jesus and their followers.
rows.anchor: عليهما السلام - وأتباعهم، عن قتادة والربيع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other reported referents are people after the messengers, the messengers' communities, or Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: من بعد الرسل، وقيل: أمم الرسل، وقيل: اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disagreement was religious: some believed and some disbelieved.
rows.anchor: في الديانات فمنهم من آمن ومنهم من كفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that the repeated statement emphasizes and draws attention to the point.
rows.anchor: قيل: تأكيدا وتنبيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view distinguishes coercion, which would remove accountability, from a command that believers refrain from fighting them.
rows.anchor: الأول مشيئة الإكراه أي لو شاء اضطرهم إلى حال يرتفع معها التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts as He wills according to the benefit required by wisdom.
rows.anchor: ولكن الله يفعل ما يريد مما هو مصلحة توجبه الحكمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other readings explain the clause as God's command to fight, or as His granting choice without coercion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يفعل ما يريد بأن يأمر بالقتال، وقيل: بأن خير وخلى، ولم يجبر ولم يكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some prophets outrank others; Muhammad is best by consensus, while the rank of any other individual prophet is not certain.
rows.anchor: لا شبهة في أن نبينا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أفضل الأنبياء، وما عداه مجوز غير مقطوع في أحد بعينه

rows.speaker: مشايخنا
rows.claim: Some of Jishumi's teachers cited Muhammad's universal mission, many followers, and finality as grounds for his superiority.
rows.anchor: من مشايخنا من ذكر فيه وجوها كثيرة نحو بعثه إلى الكافة، ولكثرة مستجيبيه، ولأنه خاتم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi says the clause opens two possible analyses: the item of comparison or evidence that comparison exists.
rows.anchor: يدل قوله: منهم من كلم الله أن يقع هناك مفاضلة ثم يحتمل وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have coerced unbelievers and prevented fighting, but coercion did not occur.
rows.anchor: تدل أنه لو شاء منع الكفار عن القتال بالإلجاء، وتدل على أن الإلجاء لم يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does whatever He wills because He is powerful in Himself and no possible act is beyond Him.
rows.anchor: يفعل ما يريد؛ لأنه قادر لذاته، لا يتعذر عليه مقدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that God wills, contrary to the Baghdadi school.
rows.anchor: وتدل أنه مريد خلاف ما تقوله البغدادية

words: لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةٌ وَلَا شَفَٰعَةٌ
rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read the three nouns in the accusative; the same construction appears in Ibrahim and al-Tur.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة بالنصب

words: لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةٌ وَلَا شَفَٰعَةٌ
rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the nominative; Jishumi explains the accusative as negation and the nominative as prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالرفع، فالنصب على النفي، والرفع على النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayʿ is exchange of goods for a price, extended figuratively to someone who trades away religion for worldly life.
rows.anchor: استبدال المتاع بالثمن، ثم يستعمل في غيره توسعا لمن باع دينه بدنياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khulla is pure affection; its root evokes a gap or opening, as if the affection cannot admit impurity.
rows.anchor: والخلة: المودة الخالصة. والخليل الخالص المودة، وأصله من الخلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shafaʿa asks on another's behalf to increase blessing or avert harm; its root suggests joining the petitioner to the person in need.
rows.anchor: وحده المسألة للغير لزيادة نعمة، أو دفع نقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting earlier peoples and establishing Muhammad's message, God urges obedience.
rows.anchor: ولما قص تعالى أخبار من مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here believing means affirming Muhammad and what he brought.
rows.anchor: صدقوا محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فيما جاء به، أنفقوا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes the spending command as obligatory alms and similar duties, since it is paired with a threat.
rows.anchor: قيل: أراد به الفرض كالزكاة ونحوها لاقتران الوعيد به، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Abu Muslim understand the command to include obligatory and voluntary spending and all good works.
rows.anchor: أراد به الفرض والنفل وسائر أعمال البر، عن ابن جريج وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الأصم وأبو علي
rows.claim: Al-Asamm and Abu Ali take the command as spending for jihad and supporting the Messenger.
rows.anchor: هي النفقة في الجهاد ومعونة الرسول، عن الأصم وأبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From what We provided you” means from what God gave you.
rows.anchor: مما رزقناكم أعطيناكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to prepare for the Day of Resurrection before it arrives.
rows.anchor: من قبل أن يأتي يوم يعني قدموا ليوم القيامة قبل إتيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There will be no trade on that day; sin makes people enemies, and another explanation is that preoccupation with oneself prevents friendship.
rows.anchor: أي لا تجارة ولا خلة أي ولا صداقة؛ لأنهم بالمعاصي يصيرون أعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denied intercession is one that would rescue them from punishment.
rows.anchor: ولا شفاعة تشفع فينجيهم من العقاب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali reads “the unbelievers” as a specific group.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم مخصوصون، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi explains the phrase as those who disbelieve in this matter being the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه الكافرون بذلك هم الظالمون عن القاضي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation calls the miser an unbeliever in generosity who wrongs the poor person.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكافر بالبخل ظالم للفقير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations call them wrongdoers for misplacing worship and wronging themselves, or for confining themselves to Hell forever.
rows.anchor: لأنهم وضعوا العبادة في غير موضعها، وظلموا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying trade, friendship, and intercession is not injustice by God; unbelievers wrong themselves through their deeds.
rows.anchor: بين أن ذلك ليس بظلم منه، بل هم الظالمون على أنفسهم بما عملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that a prophet may seek increased insight; Abraham already knew that God raises the dead.
rows.anchor: للنبي أن يلتمس زيادة البصيرة، فما يعلم لاستحالة أن يكون إبراهيم غير عالم بأنه تعالى يحيي الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Greater knowledge brings greater tranquility, contrary to those who say added knowledge has no effect and only joins necessary knowledge to inferential knowledge.
rows.anchor: زيادة العلم تقتضي زيادة سكون النفس، خلاف ما قاله بعضهم: إن زيادة العلم لا تؤثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds' separated parts returning to their wholes is a miracle that only the Knower of the unseen could accomplish.
rows.anchor: رد أبعاض كل طير إلى جملته، ولا يتأتى ذلك إلا من علام الغيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving and causing death are divine acts no one else can perform.
rows.anchor: الإحياء والإماتة، وذلك لا يقدر عليه غيره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds became discerning and answered the prayer; these events were a miracle for Abraham.
rows.anchor: أنها صارت مميزة حتى أجابت الدعاء، وكل ذلك معجزة لإبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account demonstrates Muhammad's miraculous knowledge of unseen events without reading books or associating with learned people.
rows.anchor: حيث أخبر عن أخبار غائبة من غير أن يكون قرأ كتابا ولا خالط أهل المعرفة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: If Moses asked to perceive God, the request was rejected as impossible; if he asked for necessary knowledge, it was rejected because such knowledge conflicts with continued obligation, unlike resurrection.
rows.anchor: من حمل الرؤية على الإدراك ذكر أنه سأل عن قومه، وإنما لم يجب لأنهم أحالوا في السؤال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the circumstances differed according to the interests of each time.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأن الأحوال تختلف بالمصالح في الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi cites a poetic line in which a basin speaks, as evidence for the interpretation of God's command “Be.”
rows.anchor: امتلأ الحوض وقال قطني ... مهلا رويدا قد ملأت بطني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poetic line personifies eyes as hearing and obeying, supporting the same interpretation.
rows.anchor: فقالت له العينان سمعا وطاعة ... وحدرتا كالدر لما يثقب

rows.speaker: أبو الهذيل
rows.claim: Abu al-Hudhayl says “Be” is a sign God makes for angels to know He brought about a new event; Jishumi finds this remote because the word denotes no act or kind.
rows.anchor: علامة يفعلها الله تعالى للملائكة إذا سمعوها علموا أنه أحدث أمرا، يحكى ذلك عن أبي الهذيل

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm limits the command to existing people told to become apes and similar cases; Jishumi rejects the restriction and notes that God's making them renders “Be” redundant and invites regress.
rows.anchor: هذا خاص في الموجودين الذين قال لهم: كونوا قردة، ومن جرى مجراهم، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the command address nonexistents known to God; Jishumi rejects it because nonexistents cannot be addressed and the restriction lacks evidence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنها أمر للمعدوم حيث علمه الله تعالى، وهذا فاسد؛ لأن المعدوم لا يصح خطابه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view applies the command to existing beings in reviving the dead and killing the living; Jishumi invokes the verse's generality for his stated interpretation.
rows.anchor: أمر للموجودين من إحياء الموات، وإماتة الأحياء، والآية عامة توجب حمله على ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument against God's having a child is that the originator of all things also originated Jesus without a father, and God's attributes exclude the deficiency of taking a child.
rows.anchor: مبدع الأشياء هو مبدع عيسى من غير أب. والثاني: أن من كان هذه صفاته لا يجوز عليه اتخاذ الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As creator of the heavens and earth, God is not a body, since a body cannot create a body; therefore He cannot take a child.
rows.anchor: خالق السماوات والأرض، فتدل على أنه ليس بجسم؛ لأن الجسم لا يقدر على الجسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage refutes the doctrines of the Mufawwiḍa and the Bāṭiniyya.
rows.anchor: وتدل على بطلان قول المفوضة والباطنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading includes the qibla and other matters, since its status was not established as known to them unlike the Prophet's command; they know the truth of what they concealed.
rows.anchor: عندهم بخلاف أمر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - (وهم يعلمون) صحة الأمر الذي كتموه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they know the punishment due to anyone who conceals the truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعلمون ما على من كتم حقا من العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The truth from your Lord” means what God gave Muhammad of scripture, revelation, and religious laws.
rows.anchor: يعني هو الحق من ربك، وهو ما آتاه من الكتاب والوحي والشرائع

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد وأبو علي
rows.claim: Hasan, Ibn Zayd, and Abu Ali understand the warning as concerning awareness that the earlier people knew his prophethood and qibla were true but defied and concealed them.
rows.anchor: علموا صحة نبوتك وأمر القبلة، وأنهم عاندوا وكتموا، عن الحسن وابن زيد وأبي علي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations make the warning concern doubt about the qibla, the truth of Muhammad's prophethood (the nearest view), or a matter one must know.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الشاكين في أمر القبلة، وقيل: في صحة نبوتك وهو الأقرب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the address is to someone other than the Prophet; another view addresses him though the act would not occur, as in the warning about association.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هو خطاب لغير الرسول؛ لأنه لا يشك

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa says the address includes the Prophet and others; the Prophet's freedom from doubt is what makes doubt impossible for him.
rows.anchor: وهو الأولى؛ لأنه إنما لا يجوز عليه الشك لأنه منتف عنه، عن علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi says it is permissible to forbid reprehensible acts or command duties even when God knows the person will do them.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن ينهى عن القبائح، كما يجوز أن يؤمر بالواجبات وإن علم أنه يفعل، عن القاضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage condemns defiance and warns concealers of truth, forbids doubt where knowledge is required, and confirms the Prophet's command and the qibla.
rows.anchor: قبح العناد وما يلزم كاتم الحق من الوعيد. وتدل على النهي عن الشك في المواضع التي يجب فيها العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may have capacity to do what God knows will not occur; this refutes the determinists.
rows.anchor: فتدل على أن القدرة على خلاف المعلوم جائز، وعلى ما لا يقع، فيبطل قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is accepted only when performed for God rather than for display.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن العبادة إنما تقبل إذا فعلت لله لا للرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide the unbeliever in the relevant sense, although He has shown them the truth, so the denial of guidance must be interpreted in one of the previously stated ways.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا يهدي الكافر، وقد ثبت أنه دلهم على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umma derives from aiming toward a direction and can mean community, period of time, model, stature, uprightness, or people of one religion; examples include Joseph's “after a period” and Abraham as model.
rows.anchor: وأصله القصد، يقال: أمه يؤمه أما، فالأمة الجماعة: التي تؤم جهة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khala means to be apart or alone; for something past, it evokes having vacated its place.
rows.anchor: والخلو: أصله الانفراد، يقال: خلا المكان من أهله، ويقال لما مضى: خلا؛ لأنه بمعنى خال مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kasb is an act that brings benefit or wards off harm, which is why it is not used to describe God.
rows.anchor: والكسب: العمل يجتلب به نفع أو يدفع به ضرر؛ ولذلك لا يوصف به تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One parsing makes the phrase accusative as a circumstantial clause: the community is bound to what its deeds merit.
rows.anchor: موضعه نصب على الحال، كأنه قال: ملزمة ما تستحقه بعملها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing gives the clause no syntactic position because it begins an independent sentence linked by topic, not as the prior clause's predicate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا موضع لها؛ لأنها مستأنفة، فلا تكون خبرا من المخبر عنه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling Jacob and his forefathers' religion and the People of the Book's claim to follow it, Jishumi argues against Jews and Christians; the community is Abraham and his descendants.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى ملة يعقوب وآبائه، وادعاء أهل الكتاب أنهم على دينهم، احتج عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked why women with istihada are not also avoided because of harm, Jishumi says harm describes benefit, not the legal cause; benefit may differ even when both cases involve harm.
rows.anchor: ليس ذلك بتعليل، وإنما هو بيان وجه المصلحة، ويجوز أن تختلف المصلحة في ذلك

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: On the Qadi's explanation the objection does not arise; another account says the question concerned menstruation, so the answer followed it and then explained the rulings.
rows.anchor: وعلى ما حمله القاضي لا يتوجه السؤال، وقيل: وقع عن الحيض فخرج الجواب على وفقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harath means cultivation or planting, as in “Have you considered what you cultivate?”
rows.anchor: الحرث: الزرع، ومنه: (أفرأيتم ما تحرثون) أي تزرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bishara is welcome news whose effect appears in the face.
rows.anchor: والبشارة: الخبر السار. الذي يظهر أثره في بشرة الوجه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Jabir report that Jews claimed intercourse from behind in the vagina would make a child cross-eyed; God refuted them and revealed the verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وجابر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse was revealed after Jews objected to approaching a woman standing or crouching, and God permitted it.
rows.anchor: أنكرت اليهود إتيان المرأة قائمة وباركة، فأنزل الله تعالى إباحته، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Ansar, following the Jews, objected to rear entry into the vagina, while Quraysh practiced it; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: كانت الأنصار تنكر أن يأتي الرجل المرأة من دبرها في قبلها، وكانت أخذت ذلك من اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi explain the phrase as “cultivated for you”; other renderings are “a field” or “possessor of cultivation,” with the simile particle elided.
rows.anchor: قيل: محترث لكم، عن ابن عباس والسدي. وقيل: مزرع، وقيل: ذو حرث لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the female sexual organ a field, semen seed, and a child crop is a delicate Quranic euphemism.
rows.anchor: حيث عبر بالحرث عن الفرج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as intercourse in any manner, provided it is in the place of cultivation, the vagina.
rows.anchor: أي جامعوهن كيف شئتم، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Rabi explain “how” as “from whichever direction.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: من أين شئتم، عن قتادة والربيع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the word to mean “whenever you wish”; Jishumi calls this mistaken according to the commentators.
rows.anchor: متى شئتم، عن الضحاك، وهو غلط على ما يزعم المفسرون

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab says the phrase permits choosing either withdrawal or no withdrawal.
rows.anchor: إن شئتم فاعزلوا، وإن شئتم فلا، عن سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: السدي والأصم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, al-Asamm, and Abu Muslim explain “provide for yourselves” as obeying what you have been commanded.
rows.anchor: الطاعة فيما أمرتم به واتقوا الله في مجاوزة ما حل لكم، عن السدي والأصم وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations take it as seeking offspring or marrying chaste women.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو طلب الولد، وقيل: التزوج بالعفائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You will meet Him” means fear God, knowing you will come under His judgment and authority and be repaid.
rows.anchor: يعني اتقوه عالمين أنكم صائرون إلى حكمه وسلطانه فيجازيكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says they meet God's reward for their deeds, linking back to “provide for yourselves.”
rows.anchor: ملاقو جزائه المعد على أعمالكم التي قدمتم، فهو يرجع إلى قوله: وقدموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to give glad tidings is addressed to the Messenger, who tells believers of their abundant reward for their deeds.
rows.anchor: خطاب للرسول قبلها، يعني أعلمهم بما لهم عند الله من الثواب الجزيل جزاء على أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows capacity precedes action: if one is not charged without means or wealth, a fortiori one is not charged without ability.
rows.anchor: على أن الاستطاعة قبل الفعل، وأنه إذا لم يكلف مع عدم الجدة، فلأن لا يكلف مع عدم القدرة أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human acts belong to the agent; an act created by God would not be within the agent's capacity.
rows.anchor: ما يدل أن فعل العبد فعله؛ إذ لو كان خلقا له تعالى لم يكن وسعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides what is best: mothers raise children as more affectionate and skilled, while fathers pay because they are more able.
rows.anchor: حسن نظره تعالى لعباده، وأنه يفعل لهم الأصلح حيث جعل التربية للأم؛ لأنها أشفق وأهدى للتربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At a girl's puberty the father is better suited because marriage is then at issue; for a boy at seven he is better suited to discipline.
rows.anchor: فإذا بلغ سن البنت حال البلوغ، فالأب أولى؛ لأن هذه حالة التزويج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage prohibits harming another regardless of kinship or distance, and whether the person is a child or adult.
rows.anchor: تدل على المنع من الإضرار بالغير، ويستوي فيه القريب والبعيد، والطفل والبالغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mothers have a special right to nurse; a father may not take the child from a mother who is nursing.
rows.anchor: أن للأمهات اختصاصا في الرضاع، وذلك أنها إذا أرضعت فليس للأب انتزاع الولد منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two years sets a nursing period but not an absolute duty, since completing it is conditioned on both parents' wish.
rows.anchor: على توقيت بهذه المدة، وتدل على أنه ليس بحتم؛ لذلك شرط إرادتهما إتمام الرضاعة

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد وأبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, Abu Ali, and most jurists set the nursing period that creates the marriage prohibition at two years.
rows.anchor: حولين، عن أبي يوسف ومحمد وأبي علي، وهو قول الأكثر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa allows two and a half years, adding six months because infants' needs differ between hot and cold seasons.
rows.anchor: حولين ونصفا عن أبي حنيفة؛ لأن الصبي يختلف حاله في الحر والبرد فيزيد ستة أشهر استظهارا

rows.speaker: زفر
rows.claim: Zufar sets three years because by then infants generally no longer need milk.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة أحوال، عن زفر؛ لأنه الوقت الذي تزول الحاجة إلى اللبن في الأغلب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from Aisha says adult nursing establishes the prohibition, but all jurists disagree.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عائشة أن رضاع الكبير يحرم، والفقهاء كلهم على خلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weaning before two years is permitted only after consultation and mutual agreement, so the parents can judge the child's interests.
rows.anchor: الفصال قبل الحولين لا يجوز إلا بتشاور وتراض، وفائدة المشاورة النظر في حال الصبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each parent has a right concerning nursing; mutual consent after consultation serves the child's interests.
rows.anchor: أن لكل واحد منهما حقا في الرضاع لذلك اعتبر تراضيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father bears the child's essential costs, including nursing, whether paid as a wife's maintenance or as wages to an unrelated wet nurse.
rows.anchor: ما يحتاج إليه الولد فهو على الأب؛ لأن الرضاع من أشد ما يحتاج إليه، ثم جعل ذلك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard of proper maintenance excludes extravagance and stinginess.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: بالمعروف على المنع من السرف والتقتير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the child has property, maintenance and nursing fees come from it; this differs from marital maintenance, which is compensatory.
rows.anchor: فإن كان له مال فنفقته وأجرة الرضاع في ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship maintenance is need-based benevolence and connection; if the child has no property, the father pays personally.
rows.anchor: لأن نفقة الرحم للحاجة، وهي بر وصلة، ونفقة الزوجية بمنزلة المعاوضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother has custody because nursing entails care; the maternal family has priority in care, paralleling the father's family in marriage guardianship.
rows.anchor: كان من باب الحفظ فالأم أولى، وقد ذكرنا التقدير

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The custody ages stated for Abu Hanifa are seven years for a boy and, for a girl, when she reaches the age of women.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا التقدير فيدل على ما قاله أبو حنيفة في الغلام سبع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maintenance obligations account for the payer's means; imposing them on the destitute as charity would imply an unsound reciprocal obligation.
rows.anchor: النفقة يعتبر فيها اليسار؛ إذ لو جاز إيجابه على المعسر صلة لأوجب له أيضا، وهذا فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse permits hiring someone other than the mother to nurse the child.
rows.anchor: جواز استرضاع غير الأم، وجواز الاستئجار عليه

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi says a nursing wife in her waiting period may receive marital or waiting-period maintenance as well as nursing wages.
rows.anchor: يجمع بين نفقة الزوجية وأجرة الرضاع، وكذلك بين نفقة العدة والرضاع، وهو اختيار القاضي

rows.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: The Hanafi companions deny separate nursing wages when the woman already receives marital or waiting-period maintenance.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال: لا تجب نفقة الرضاع؛ لأنه وجبت نفقة الزوجية والعدة، وهو قول أصحاب أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi refers readers to legal works for detailed rules of family maintenance and nursing.
rows.anchor: وتفصيل نفقة الأقارب ومسائل الرضاع كتب الفقه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Abu Bakr from Asim read the verb with doubled open t and h; Jishumi says this means the women bathe.
rows.anchor: قرأ: يطهرن بفتح الطاء والهاء والتشديد: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the lighter form, explained by Hasan and al-Farra as the cessation of menstruation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتخفيف فمعنى التشديد يغتسلن، ومعنى التخفيف ينقطع حيضهن، عن الحسن والفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word covers menstruation and its place; blood gathers there as water gathers in a basin. Menstruation occurs at known times, while istihada is outside them.
rows.anchor: والحيض اجتماع الدم إلى ذلك المكان، ومنه يسمى الحوض لاجتماع الماء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Menstrual bleeding at known times is menstruation; bleeding outside those days is istihada, making the woman mustahada.
rows.anchor: فإذا سال في غير أيام معلومة قيل: استحيضت فهي مستحاضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtizal means withdrawing or moving away; Jishumi compares the usage in the Cave youths' story and Abraham's withdrawal.
rows.anchor: والاعتزال: التنحي عن الشيء، وكل شيء نحيته فقد عزلته

rows.speaker: قتادة عن الحسن
rows.claim: One account says Amr ibn Ubayd withdrew from al-Hasan's circle, after which Qatada said the Mu'tazila were named from this act.
rows.anchor: لأن عمرو بن عبيد تنحى عن حلقة الحسن، فقال قتادة: لما فعلت المعتزلة سموا بذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account derives the Mu'tazila's name from Wasil ibn Ata's withdrawal from disputed positions over the intermediate status.
rows.anchor: لأن واصل بن عطاء اعتزل أقوال المختلفين في المنزلة بين المنزلتين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third account says they were named for withdrawing from innovations and doubts, following the straight path and defending religion.
rows.anchor: لأنهم اعتزلوا كل بدعة، وتجنبوا كل شبهة، وقاموا على سواء السبيل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Jishumi cites a report attributed to the Prophet that whoever withdraws from evil falls into good; he gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من اعتزل من الشر سقط في الخير

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Jishumi cites a report attributed to the Prophet that the community will split into more than seventy groups and the best and most pious is the Mu'tazila; he gives no grading.
rows.anchor: روي: ستفترق أمتي على بضع وسبعين فرقة أبرها وأتقاها الفئة المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭuhr is the opposite of dirt; purification may mean avoiding sin. Ṭahur can mean water, pure, or purifying; Thaʿlab says it is both pure and purifying.
rows.anchor: والطهر: خلاف الدنس، والتطهر: التنزه عن الإثم، والطهور: الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tatahharat means a woman washed; ṭahurat means her blood stopped. Forms with open or rounded h can mean the same, though the rounded form may be intransitive.
rows.anchor: وتطهرت المرأة اغتسلت، وطهرت تطهر إذا انقطع دمها فهي طاهر بلا هاء
